# Grouped line graphs {#sec-grp-line-graphs}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(patchwork)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_snick(
    base_size = 12))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_snick()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_snick()`, built from Nickelodeon's Saturday night block (SNICK): a night purple background, a Nickelodeon orange frame and title, slime green, purple, blue, yellow, and pink marks, and an Arial Black title.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(patchwork)
set.seed(1992)
nick_ratings <- tibble(
  date = seq(as.Date("1993-01-01"), as.Date("1999-12-31"), by = "day")) |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day_of_week = factor(wday(date, label = TRUE), ordered = FALSE),
    day_category = if_else(day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
                           "Weekend", "Weekday"),
    yr_mnth = floor_date(date, unit = "month"),
    yr_qtr = factor(paste0(year, "/0", quarter(date)), ordered = TRUE),
    night_avg = c(Sun = 3.0, Mon = 2.4, Tue = 2.3, Wed = 2.3,
                  Thu = 2.4, Fri = 2.8, Sat = 4.2)[as.character(day_of_week)],
    trend = 0.25 * (year - 1993) - 0.04 * (year - 1993)^2,
    summer = 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * (month - 4) / 12),
    rating = round(rnorm(n(), mean = night_avg + trend + summer,
                         sd = 0.35), 2)) |>
  select(-night_avg, -trend, -summer)
# basic_line ----
avg_rating_day_cat_yr <- nick_ratings |>
    group_by(year, day_category) |>
    summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |>
    ungroup()
basic_line <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_day_cat_yr,
       mapping = aes(x = year, y = avg_rating, group = day_category)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_category), linewidth = 1)
# grp_line ----
avg_rating_dow_qtr <- nick_ratings |>
    filter(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997) |>
    group_by(yr_qtr, day_of_week) |>
    summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |>
    ungroup()
grp_line <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_dow_qtr,
       mapping = aes(x = yr_qtr, y = avg_rating, group = day_of_week)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week), linewidth = 1)
# pal_line ----
avg_rating_dow_mnth <- nick_ratings |>
    filter(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997) |>
    group_by(yr_mnth, day_of_week) |>
    summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |>
    ungroup()
pal_line <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_dow_mnth,
       mapping = aes(x = yr_mnth, y = avg_rating, group = day_of_week,
                     color = day_of_week)) +
    geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth,
                  day_of_week %in% c("Mon", "Thu", "Fri")),
              alpha = 1 / 4, linewidth = 0.85) +
    geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth,
                  day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun")),
              alpha = 1 / 2, linewidth = 0.75, linetype = "longdash") +
    geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth,
                  day_of_week %in% c("Tue", "Wed")),
              linewidth = 1.25)
# facet_line ----
facet_line <- ggplot(data = filter(nick_ratings, date >= as.Date("1998-07-01")),
       mapping = aes(x = date, y = rating, group = day_of_week)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week)) +
    facet_grid(day_of_week ~ day_category)
# final graphs ----
mini_theme <- theme(axis.text = element_blank(),
                    axis.title = element_blank(),
                    strip.text = element_blank(),
                    legend.position = "none",
                    plot.background = element_rect(linewidth = 2))
basic_line + grp_line + pal_line + facet_line +
    patchwork::plot_layout(nrow = 2) &
    mini_theme
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (continuous) variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a numeric (date) variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ at least one categorical variable**
:::

::::

## Description

A grouped line graph shows how a number changes over time, with one line for each group.[^grp-line] We can tell one line from another by color, by how each line looks, or by putting each group in its own small graph.[^styles]

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Bring in the code we'll use.[^packages]


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_line_graph
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for tibble() and data manipulation
library(lubridate) # for working with dates
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

Nickelodeon makes shows for kids, and SNICK was the set of shows it put on one night each week. Every Saturday night starting in 1992, kids watched SNICK (*Clarissa Explains It All*, *Are You Afraid of the Dark?*, and *All That*).[^couch] A rating is a number that says how many out of every 100 homes were watching. We'll make up[^simulate] a rating for Nickelodeon[^nielsen] for every day from 1993 through 1999. Each night of the week gets its own average (`night_avg`), with Saturday on top. Two changes that move little by little get added to the average for each night: a `trend` that goes up through the middle of the 1990s and comes down near the end, and a `summer` change that goes up when school is out. Then `rnorm()` adds a small change that is different every day.[^noise] Starting with `set.seed()`[^seed] means you'll get the same `r scales::comma(nrow(nick_ratings))` days every time you run the code below.

We'll also make the date columns we need for the groups.[^date-vars] A quarter is three months, or one of four parts of a year.

  - `day_of_week` (a column of groups from `wday()`,[^factor] with no order set, so the graphs use the colors that come with the look[^theme]) and `day_category` (`"Weekday"` or `"Weekend"`)

  - `yr_mnth` (the first day of each month) and `yr_qtr` (the year and quarter)

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_nick_ratings
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1992) # same daily ratings every time the code runs
nick_ratings <- tibble(
  date = seq(as.Date("1993-01-01"), as.Date("1999-12-31"), by = "day") # every day from 1993 to 1999
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day_of_week = factor(wday(date, label = TRUE), ordered = FALSE), # Sun through Sat
    day_category = if_else(day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun"),
                           "Weekend", "Weekday"),
    yr_mnth = floor_date(date, unit = "month"), # first day of each month
    yr_qtr = factor(paste0(year, "/0", quarter(date)), ordered = TRUE), # year and quarter
    night_avg = c(Sun = 3.0, Mon = 2.4, Tue = 2.3, Wed = 2.3, # average rating for each night
                  Thu = 2.4, Fri = 2.8, Sat = 4.2)[as.character(day_of_week)], # (Saturday is SNICK night)
    trend = 0.25 * (year - 1993) - 0.04 * (year - 1993)^2, # ratings rise, then fall
    summer = 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * (month - 4) / 12), # summer bump when school is out
    rating = round(
      rnorm(n(), mean = night_avg + trend + summer, # add the three parts together
            sd = 0.35), # plus random night to night noise
      2 # two decimal places
      )
    ) |>
  select(-night_avg, -trend, -summer) # drop the helper columns
glimpse(nick_ratings)
```
:::

We'll use these data in the *More info* section for more line graphs, but for now:

  - Put the rows of `nick_ratings` into groups by `year` and `day_category`

  - Work out the average `rating` for each group as `avg_rating`

  - Keep the data in `avg_rating_day_cat_yr`.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_avg_rating_day_cat_yr
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
avg_rating_day_cat_yr <- nick_ratings |>
    group_by(year, day_category) |> # one group per year for weekdays and weekends
    summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |> # average rating in each group
    ungroup()
glimpse(avg_rating_day_cat_yr)
```
:::

## Distribution

A grouped line graph almost never shows each number by itself.[^raw] It shows an *average* for each group at each point in time, and averages act in a very different way from the numbers they come from. Below we'll move from the ratings for each day, to a graph, to the rule behind it,[^formula] and see why averages make the differences between groups easy to see.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the first week of 1996.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_grp_line
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
nick_ratings |>
  filter(year == 1996) |>
  select(date, day_of_week, rating) |>
  head(7)
```
:::

Saturday is far on top this week, but the other nights are close enough that their order could change next week.[^weeknights] Below we find how many of each night there are in 1996 and work out the mean and how far ratings usually fall from it (`sd`)[^sd] for each night of the week.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_grp_line
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
nick_1996 <- nick_ratings |>
  filter(year == 1996) |>
  group_by(day_of_week) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(rating), sd = sd(rating))
nick_1996
```
:::

Each night of the week comes up `r min(nick_1996$n)` or `r max(nick_1996$n)` times in a year. The Saturday mean (`r round(nick_1996$mean[nick_1996$day_of_week == "Sat"], 2)`) is well above the Tuesday mean (`r round(nick_1996$mean[nick_1996$day_of_week == "Tue"], 2)`), but the rating for any one night moves about `r round(mean(nick_1996$sd), 1)` points away from its mean.[^sd-night]

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The graph below shows every Tuesday and Saturday rating from 1996 as a light line we can see through,[^alpha] then adds the average for each month as a wide line. The lines for each day go up and down a lot, while the lines for each month move much less.[^zigzag]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_grp_line
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
tue_sat_1996 <- nick_ratings |>
  filter(year == 1996, day_of_week %in% c("Tue", "Sat"))
tue_sat_monthly <- tue_sat_1996 |>
  group_by(yr_mnth, day_of_week) |>
  summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = tue_sat_1996,
            aes(x = date, y = rating, color = day_of_week),
            alpha = 1 / 3) +
  geom_line(data = tue_sat_monthly,
            aes(x = yr_mnth + 14, y = avg_rating, color = day_of_week), # middle of each month
            linewidth = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "1996", y = "Rating", color = "Night")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

A hill is a line that is high in the middle and low on both sides. Each day's rating is picked from a [hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution)[^normal] with its middle at that night's average for that time of year:

$$
\text{rating}_d \sim \text{Normal}\left(\mu_{\text{night}} + \text{trend}_{\text{year}} + \text{summer}_{\text{month}}, \; \sigma = 0.35\right)
$$

When we take the average of $n$ picks, how far the average usually falls from its middle is $\sigma / \sqrt{n}$.[^se] An average of about four Saturdays for one month moves by about $0.35 / \sqrt{4} \approx 0.18$ points. Each `avg_rating` point for one year below is an average of about 104 weekend nights or 261 other nights, so it moves by only $0.35 / \sqrt{104} \approx 0.03$ or $0.35 / \sqrt{261} \approx 0.02$ points. That's why the lines for each year move so little, and why the space between weekdays and weekends is easy to see. The `sd` column in **COUNT IT** is a little larger than 0.35 because it also has the `summer` change in it. Try changing `sd = 0.35` to `sd = 1`, and watch the lines for each day in **DRAW IT** become hard to follow,[^tangle] while the lines for each year move very little.

## Grammar

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

  - Make the words around the graph[^labels] with `labs()`

  - Put `year` on the `x` axis and `avg_rating` on the `y` axis, and join `day_category` to `group`[^map]

  - Add the `geom_line()` part of the graph[^layer] and give each `day_category` its own color (*inside* `aes()`)[^color]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_line
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_line_graph <- labs(title = "Nickelodeon ratings",
                        caption = "Simulated data",
                        subtitle = "1993-1999",
                        y = "Average rating",
                        x = "Year",
                        color = "Day Category")

ggp2_line <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_day_cat_yr,
       mapping = aes(x = year,
                     y = avg_rating,
                     group = day_category)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_category))
ggp2_line +
    labs_line_graph
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_line
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_line_graph <- labs(title = "Nickelodeon ratings",
                        caption = "Simulated data",
                        subtitle = "1993-1999",
                        y = "Average rating",
                        x = "Year",
                        color = "Day Category")

ggp2_line <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_day_cat_yr,
       mapping = aes(x = year,
                     y = avg_rating,
                     group = day_category)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_category))
ggp2_line +
    labs_line_graph
```


## More info

Line graphs work well for showing how numbers change for many groups.[^relationships] We can also break the graph into small graphs to compare many groups at once.[^facets]

### Groups

In the last graph, we can see the ratings are highest around `1996` or `1997`.[^peak]

  - We'll make another set of averages from `nick_ratings`, but this time we keep only the ratings from `1996` and `1997`[^summarized]

  - Put the rows into groups by `yr_qtr` and `day_of_week`

  - Then work out the average `rating` for each group as `avg_rating`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: avg_rating_dow_qtr
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
avg_rating_dow_qtr <- nick_ratings |>
    filter(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997) |>
    group_by(yr_qtr, day_of_week) |>
    summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |>
    ungroup()
glimpse(avg_rating_dow_qtr)
```
:::

Now when we make our line graph, we will have a column with seven groups (`day_of_week`):[^levels]

  + Make the second title[^subtitle] with `paste0()`, so it stays right if the data under it changes.

  +  Put the name of each night at the end of its line with `geom_text_repel()` (from `ggrepel`), and turn off the key that tells us which color goes with which night[^legend] with `theme(legend.position = "none")` (so we don't have to look from the key to the lines and back).

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: labs_line_graph_grp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
# here we create the labels (with the subtitle updating with the data)
labs_line_graph_grp <- labs(title = "Nickelodeon ratings",
                        caption = "Simulated data",
                        subtitle = paste0("Between ",
                                    min(avg_rating_dow_qtr$yr_qtr),
                                    " and ",
                                    max(avg_rating_dow_qtr$yr_qtr)),
                        y = "Average rating",
                        x = "Year/Quarter",
                        color = "Day of Week")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_grp
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.75
# Build layer with yr_qtr and day_of_week
ggp2_line_grp <- ggplot(data = avg_rating_dow_qtr,
                   mapping = aes(x = yr_qtr,
                                 y = avg_rating,
                                 group = day_of_week)) +
        geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week))
# name each line at its end, in place of the legend
ggp2_line_grp +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
        data = filter(avg_rating_dow_qtr, yr_qtr == max(yr_qtr)),
        aes(label = day_of_week, color = day_of_week),
        hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.2, direction = "y",
        segment.color = NA) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.5, 1))) +
    labs_line_graph_grp +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```
:::

The Saturday line is on top in every quarter (that's SNICK), and every night goes up and comes down with the `summer` change.

### Line Styles

  - We can make the lines in our graph easier to tell from each other by changing how each line looks (`linetype` and `linewidth`),[^line-style] or by changing how much we can see through all of them (`alpha`).[^opacity]

  - We'll work through some examples below with another part of `nick_ratings`.[^subset]

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: avg_rating_dow_mnth
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false
avg_rating_dow_mnth <- nick_ratings |>
    filter(year >= 1996 & year <= 1997) |>
    group_by(yr_mnth, day_of_week) |>
    summarise(avg_rating = mean(rating)) |>
    ungroup()
glimpse(avg_rating_dow_mnth)
```
:::



::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: labs_line_styles
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
labs_line_styles <- labs(
    title = "Nickelodeon ratings",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = paste0(
        "Between ",
        min(avg_rating_dow_mnth$yr_mnth),
        " and ",
        max(avg_rating_dow_mnth$yr_mnth)
    ),
    y = "Average rating",
    x = "Year-Month",
    color = "Day of Week"
)
```
:::


### `alpha` & `linewidth`

Changing how lines look is a good way to make some lines stand out more than others.[^highlight]

  - We'll start by making one part of the graph[^layer] with lines for Monday (`"Mon"`), Thursday (`"Thu"`), and Friday (`"Fri"`), and use `alpha` to set how much we can see through them.[^opacity]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.75
ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri <-
    ggplot(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth,
        day_of_week %in% c("Mon", "Thu", "Fri"))) +
    geom_line(
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = avg_rating,
            group = day_of_week,
            color = day_of_week),
        alpha = 1 / 4,
        linewidth = 0.85)
# layer 1
ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri +
    labs_line_styles +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
```
:::


### `linetype`

Then we'll change the `linetype` of Saturday and Sunday to `"longdash"` (and give them a little higher `alpha`, so we can see through them *a little* less).[^transparent]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_sat_sun
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.75
ggp2_line_sat_sun <- ggp2_line_mon_thu_fri +
    geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth,
            day_of_week %in% c("Sat", "Sun")),
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = avg_rating,
            group = day_of_week,
            color = day_of_week),
        alpha = 1 / 2,
        linewidth = 0.75,
        linetype = "longdash")
# layers 1 & 2
ggp2_line_sat_sun +
    labs_line_styles +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
```
:::

### Color palettes

  - Add `geom_line()` for Tuesday and Wednesday, and choose the colors by hand with `scale_color_manual()` (below we use a list of SNICK colors, each with the name of its night).[^named-vector]

  - We also set the order of the key by hand, by giving `breaks` the order the groups first had.[^legend-order]


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_pal_d
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.75
# original factor levels
lev_order <- levels(avg_rating_dow_mnth$day_of_week)
# SNICK colors
snick_pal <- c(Sun = "#FF5FA2", Mon = "#29B6F6", Tue = "#8CC63F",
               Wed = "#FFD200", Thu = "#B07CE8", Fri = "#F4F1FA",
               Sat = "#F57D0D")
# layer 3
ggp2_line_pal_d <- ggp2_line_sat_sun +
    # add line
    geom_line(data = filter(avg_rating_dow_mnth,
            day_of_week %in% c("Tue", "Wed")),
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = avg_rating,
            group = day_of_week,
            color = day_of_week),
        linewidth = 1.25) +
    # add palette
    scale_color_manual(
        breaks = lev_order,
        # original factor levels
        values = snick_pal)
# three layers
ggp2_line_pal_d +
    # labels
    labs_line_styles +
    # legend position
    theme(legend.position = "top")
```
:::


Changing how the lines look is a good way to make some lines stand out more than others.

### Labels

We'll put words on the graph[^geom-label] to show the highest rating for one day and the highest average rating for one month, for a few nights of the week.

  - To do this, we're going to make two small tables of words, `label_max_dow` and `label_max_avg_dow`, that we'll use to name the highest values.[^max]

  - Each has a row for every night of the week (`label_max_dow` has one more, because the highest Sunday rating, 4.4, came on two days: `1996-08-11` and `1997-04-20`) and a column of words (`lbl`) that we can use with `geom_label()`.[^lbl]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: label_max_dow
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
label_max_dow <- nick_ratings |>
    group_by(day_of_week) |>
    summarise(max_rating = max(rating)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    inner_join(y = nick_ratings,
        by = c("max_rating" = "rating", "day_of_week")) |>
    mutate(lbl = paste0(day_of_week,
        " (", date, "), max rating = ", max_rating)) |>
    select(day_of_week, yr_mnth, max_rating, lbl)

arrange(label_max_dow, desc(max_rating)) |>
    slice(1:2)
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: label_max_avg_dow
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
label_max_avg_dow <- avg_rating_dow_mnth |>
    # group by sun-sat
    group_by(day_of_week) |>
    # get max avg
    slice_max(order_by = avg_rating, n = 1) |>
    # ungroup
    ungroup() |>
    rename(max_avg_rating = avg_rating) |>
    mutate(lbl = paste0(day_of_week,
        ": max avg rating = ", round(max_avg_rating, 2)))
arrange(label_max_avg_dow, desc(max_avg_rating)) |>
    slice(1:2)
```
:::

Now that we have a table of words for each number, we can keep only the days we want to name.[^filter-lbl]

  - We'll use `filter()` to get the highest values for `"Wed"` (in `label_max_wed_dow` and `label_max_avg_wed_dow`)

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: label_max_wed
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
# get wed
label_max_wed_dow <- label_max_dow |>
    filter(day_of_week == "Wed")
label_max_wed_dow
label_max_avg_wed_dow <- label_max_avg_dow |>
    filter(day_of_week == "Wed")
label_max_avg_wed_dow
```
:::


Add `geom_point()` and `geom_label()` for Wednesday.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_wed_labels
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.75
# point for max rating
ggp2_line_wed_max_pnts <- geom_point(
    data = label_max_wed_dow,
    aes(x = yr_mnth,
        y = max_rating,
        color = day_of_week),
    size = 2.5,
    show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_pnts <-
    geom_point(
        data = label_max_avg_wed_dow,
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = max_avg_rating,
            color = day_of_week),
        size = 2.5,
        alpha = 1/2,
        show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_wed_max_lbl <- geom_label(
    data = label_max_wed_dow,
    aes(x = yr_mnth,
        y = max_rating,
        label = lbl,
        color = day_of_week),
    fill = "#1E1238",
    nudge_y = 0.25,
    nudge_x = 60,
    size = 2.5,
    show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_lbl <-
    geom_label(data = label_max_avg_wed_dow,
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = max_avg_rating,
            label = lbl,
            color = day_of_week),
        fill = "#1E1238",
        nudge_y = -0.35,
        nudge_x = 60,
        size = 2.5,
        show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_pal_d +
    ggp2_line_wed_max_pnts +
    ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_pnts +
    ggp2_line_wed_max_lbl +
    ggp2_line_wed_max_avg_lbl +
    # add labels
    labs_line_styles +
    # move legend to top
    theme(legend.position = "top")
```
:::


We'll use `filter()` to get the highest values for `"Tue"` (in `label_max_tue_dow` and `label_max_avg_tue_dow`):

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: label_max_tue
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
# get tue
label_max_tue_dow <- label_max_dow |>
    filter(day_of_week == "Tue")
label_max_tue_dow
label_max_avg_tue_dow <- label_max_avg_dow |>
    filter(day_of_week == "Tue")
label_max_avg_tue_dow
```
:::


Add `geom_point()` and `geom_label()` for Tuesday

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_tue_labels
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.75
# point for max rating
ggp2_line_tue_max_pnts <-
    geom_point(data = label_max_tue_dow,
        aes(x = yr_mnth,

            color = day_of_week),
        size = 2.5,
        show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_tue_max_avg_pnts <-
    geom_point(
        data = label_max_avg_tue_dow,
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = max_avg_rating,
            color = day_of_week),
        size = 2.5,
        alpha = 1/2,
        show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_tue_max_lbl <-
    geom_label(data = label_max_tue_dow,
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = max_rating,
            label = lbl,
            color = day_of_week),
        fill = "#1E1238",
        nudge_y = 0.25,
        nudge_x = -60,
        size = 2.5,
        show.legend = FALSE)

ggp2_line_tue_max_avg_lbl <-
    geom_label(data = label_max_avg_tue_dow,
        aes(x = yr_mnth,
            y = max_avg_rating,
            label = lbl,
            color = day_of_week),
        fill = "#1E1238",
        nudge_y = -0.35,
        nudge_x = -60,

ggp2_line_pal_d +
    # wednesday layers
    ggp2_line_wed_max_pnts +

    ggp2_line_wed_max_lbl +

    # tuesday layers
```

:::

See how the highest ratings for one day are well above the highest averages for one month. One night can be very high by chance, but an average of four or five nights almost never is[^lucky] (just like we saw in the **Distribution** section).

### Facets

Last, we can use small graphs to see each of the lines on its own.[^facets]

  - We'll make a set of data with the rating for each day from `1998-07-01` to `1999-12-31` and keep it as `daily_ratings_9899`


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: daily_ratings_9899
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
daily_ratings_9899 <- nick_ratings |>
    filter(date >= as.Date("1998-07-01")) |>
    select(date, day_category, day_of_week, rating)
glimpse(daily_ratings_9899)
```
:::


- `facet_wrap()` with one column of groups (`var ~ .`) makes a small graph for each group, while `facet_grid()` makes a table of small graphs, with the groups of one column down the side and the groups of another across the top (written as `var ~ var`).[^facet-grid]

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_facet_wrap
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 0.8
# labels
labs_line_graph_facet_wrap <- labs(
    title = "Nickelodeon ratings",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = paste0(
        "Between ",
        min(daily_ratings_9899$date),
        " and ",
        max(daily_ratings_9899$date)
    ),
    y = "Rating",
    x = "Date",
    color = "Day of Week"
)
# layer
ggp2_line_facet_wrap <- ggplot(data = daily_ratings_9899,
    mapping = aes(x = date,
        y = rating,
        group = day_of_week)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = snick_pal) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(2, 3, 4, 5)) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year",
        date_labels = "%Y") +
    facet_wrap(day_of_week ~ .)

ggp2_line_facet_wrap +
    labs_line_graph_facet_wrap +
    theme(legend.position = "none") # the small graph names already say which night
```
:::


  - It's always a good idea to check the words and numbers along the `x` and `y` axes when we use small graphs.[^axis-text] I've changed the `x` and `y` axes above with `scale_y_continuous()` and `scale_x_date()` before adding `facet_wrap()`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: ggp2_line_facet_grid
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| fig-asp: 1
# labels
labs_line_graph_facet_grid <- labs(
    title = "Nickelodeon ratings",
    caption = "Simulated data",
    subtitle = paste0(
        "Between ",
        min(daily_ratings_9899$date),
        " and ",
        max(daily_ratings_9899$date)
    ),
    y = "Rating",
    x = "Date",
    color = "Day of Week"
)
# layer
ggp2_line_facet_grid <- ggplot(data = daily_ratings_9899,
    mapping = aes(x = date,
        y = rating,
        group = day_of_week)) +
    geom_line(aes(color = day_of_week)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = snick_pal) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(2, 3, 4, 5)) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year",
        date_labels = "%Y") +
    facet_grid(day_of_week ~ day_category)

ggp2_line_facet_grid +
    labs_line_graph_facet_grid
```
:::

Seven of the 14 small graphs have no line, because each night of the week is in only one of the two groups (`Weekday` or `Weekend`).

We chose the colors by hand with `scale_color_manual()` and the `snick_pal` list of named colors we made in the *Color palettes* section.[^named-vector]

[^grp-line]: Grouped line graphs show group changes over time for a continuous variable across categorical levels.

[^styles]: Color, line style, and faceting.

[^packages]: Install and load the packages.

[^simulate]: Simulate.

[^nielsen]: A Nielsen style rating.

[^noise]: Day to day noise: `rnorm()` draws each rating from a normal distribution with `sd = 0.35`.

[^seed]: Setting the random seed.

[^date-vars]: The date variables we need for grouping.

[^couch]: Kids parked themselves in front of SNICK and the orange couch.

[^factor]: A factor.

[^theme]: Unordered, so the graphs use the theme colors.

[^raw]: A grouped line graph rarely plots raw values.

[^formula]: The formula.

[^weeknights]: The weeknights.

[^sd]: The standard deviation.

[^sd-night]: Any single night wanders about this many rating points from its mean (the average of the seven standard deviations).

[^alpha]: A thin, faded (partially transparent) line.

[^zigzag]: The daily lines zig and zag.

[^normal]: A [normal distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_distribution) centered on that night's average for that time of year.

[^se]: The standard deviation of an average of $n$ draws is the [standard error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_error).

[^tangle]: Turn into a tangle.

[^labels]: Labels.

[^layer]: The layer.

[^map]: Map `year` to `x`, `avg_rating` to `y`, and `day_category` to `group`.

[^color]: Map `day_category` to the `color` aesthetic.

[^relationships]: Line graphs are great for displaying relationships across variables with multiple groups (or levels).

[^facets]: Facets (small multiples).

[^peak]: The ratings peak.

[^summarized]: Another summarized dataset, with the observations restricted to the ratings between 1996 and 1997.

[^levels]: A categorical variable with seven levels.

[^subtitle]: The subtitle.

[^legend]: The legend.

[^line-style]: The line style.

[^opacity]: The opacity.

[^subset]: Another subset.

[^highlight]: Line styles are an excellent tool for highlighting or emphasizing certain lines over others.

[^transparent]: Somewhat transparent, with a slightly higher `alpha`.

[^named-vector]: A named vector.

[^legend-order]: Supplying the original factor levels to the `breaks` argument sets the legend order.

[^geom-label]: Labels made with `geom_label()`.

[^max]: The maximum values.

[^lbl]: A label variable (`lbl`).

[^filter-lbl]: Filter the label tables for each metric to the days we want to label.

[^facet-grid]: `facet_wrap()` with a single categorical variable creates a plot for each discrete level, while `facet_grid()` creates a grid of plots, one for each pair of levels from two variables.

[^lucky]: A single night can get lucky.

[^axis-text]: The axis text.
